title: Controlled synthesis of yolk–shell structured silica nanoparticles under microwave irradiation
content: A simple and efficient sol–gel method was adopted to prepare yolk–shell structured silica nanoparticles (YSNPs). Using in situ synthesized phenolic resin microspheres as templates and tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) as the silicon source, silica nanoparticles with different morphologies can be controllably prepared by precisely tuning the microwave synthesis temperature. The yolk–shell structured nanoparticles have a high specific surface area of up to 570 m2 g−1 and a pore volume of 0.79 cm3 g−1. Mechanistic studies suggested that the pore volume of the phenolic resin template and the content of polar functional groups on its surface jointly influence the morphological evolution of YSNPs. In addition, the yolk–shell structured nanoparticles can be used for loading a Ziegler–Natta catalyst.
